raw_comment: From this graph, I noticed that the areas of land with extreme or exceptional drought tend to be more toward the Midwest. I also noticed that the areas with abnormally dry or moderately dry land areas are more so on the east and west coasts. I think this is because the coasts are close to a source of water making it harder for the land in that region to become severally dry. I wonder how there are so many wildfires throughout California if it's near a body of water and most of the state is abnormally dry. Another thing I wonder is how can we prevent these droughts from happening. This relates to me and my community because New York is relatively fine when it comes to droughts so we should consider our acts to prevent it from progressing into something we cannot control. A catchy headline to go with the article would be "A Visual View of Droughts Throughout America".
